facts.P1_fx_receipts: Yes, but under CEMAC exchange control; repatriate earnings through your bank.
facts.P2_fcy_account: No: residents can't open foreign-currency accounts locally; declare accounts abroad.
facts.P3_local_gateways: Mobile-money merchant accounts reportedly need RCCM and NIU registration.
facts.L1_registration: Register an individual enterprise at the CFCE one-stop shop, about FCFA 46,500.
facts.L2_tax_id: NIU taxpayer number, online-only via the DGI using your ID card number.
facts.L3_income_tax_foreign: Up to FCFA 50m turnover, the IGS single tax replaces income tax and VAT.
facts.L4_vat_gst: 19.25% VAT; IGS taxpayers don't charge it; exports are zero-rated.
facts.L5_data_protection: Data protection law 2024/017, in force since June 2026.
facts.L6_consumer_ecommerce: Buyers can withdraw within 15 days of receiving goods.
facts.L7_incentives: The IGS single tax up to FCFA 50m is the main simplification.

watch_out.text: PayPal balances can't be withdrawn to Cameroonian banks.
Declare any accounts you hold abroad to the BEAC.
